title: A Extraction for the Cipher
premise: Mirabel Joubert, a financial-crimes investigator who launders reputations for the powerful, is approached by a stranger claiming she once did him a favor she has no memory of — and that the interest on that debt is now due. The favor was orchestrated by her late mother, a cipher clerk whose hidden network of obligations Mirabel has unknowingly inherited. To pay it, she must extract Anton Voss, a defector holding the ledger of everyone the network ever bought, from a hostile consulate before dawn — while discovering Voss may be bait set by the very people her mother's cipher was built to trap. In the climax, Mirabel chooses to burn the ledger rather than sell it, severing her inheritance but keeping the found family the extraction team becomes; the epilogue finds her working cases no one wants attributed, but no longer alone.
about_author: I. M. Ashgrove is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through jurisdictions that officially don't exist with each other. They write thrillers about people who keep other people's secrets for a living.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A stranger named Callum Rook appears at her office claiming she saved his life in Lisbon — a trip she never took — and that the debt is now callable. He leaves a key to a safety deposit box in her mother's name. Emotional beat: uncanny dread beneath her controlled professional surface.

chapters.title: Inheritance in a Steel Drawer
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The deposit box holds her mother's cipher book: coded records of favors owed across decades, including one marked payable to 'C.R., Lisbon.' Mirabel realizes her mother ran an underground exchange of obligations. Emotional beat: grief reframed as discovery; the mother she knew doubles before her eyes.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Her firm's biggest client, Halvard Group, surfaces in the cipher as a debtor — and someone at work notices her inquiries. Her mentor, Odile, warns her off with unusual urgency. Emotional beat: paranoia entering the sanctuary of her career.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV Callum. Rook explains the debt: the network extracted him once, and now it must extract again — Anton Voss, a defector hiding in a coastal consulate with a ledger naming every cipher member alive. Refusal means exposure. Emotional beat: reluctant recruitment; the first spark of trust between strangers bound by a dead woman.

chapters.title: The Crew of Debts
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. She meets the extraction team: a disgraced pilot, a forger who owes the network three favors, and Rook himself — all people her mother's cipher once rescued. She is among people shaped like her. Emotional beat: belonging arriving sideways, disguised as a job.

chapters.title: Consulate Nights
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Surveillance of the consulate reveals Voss moves freely — too freely. Mirabel's analysis shows his security pattern is choreographed, a stage set. Someone wants them to come. Emotional beat: the plan curdling into suspicion; competence as both weapon and warning.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: POV Callum. Rook confesses the Halvard Group offered him everything he's lost if he delivers Voss — and Mirabel — to them. He hasn't decided. Emotional beat: betrayal hovering over loyalty; the found family tested by the oldest currency, self-preservation.

chapters.title: Bait Before Dawn
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The team launches the extraction anyway, choosing each other over safety. Inside the consulate, Mirabel confirms Voss is bait — Halvard's men wait at the airstrip. She improvises a second route while the pilot holds the plane against orders. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve; the crew becoming family under fire.

chapters.title: The Burning Page
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Cornered at the airfield, Mirabel faces Halvard's broker, who offers her the empire her mother built — the ledger, the debts, the power. She burns the cipher book page by page as the plane lifts off, freeing every debtor including herself. Emotional beat: climax; renunciation as victory, inheritance refused to be kept whole.

chapters.title: Cases No One Wants Attributed
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Weeks later: Voss resettled, Odile quietly exposed, Rook staying 'until the coffee runs out.' Mirabel takes a new unattributable case — and her crew shows up without being asked. Emotional beat: resolution; belonging no longer inherited but chosen.
